title: A false witness makes a universal test fail
statement: Let $l$ be a list of elements of a type $\alpha$ and let $p \colon \alpha \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ be a Boolean predicate. If some element $a$ of $l$ satisfies $p(a) = \mathrm{false}$, then the test whether every entry of $l$ satisfies $p$ evaluates to $\mathrm{false}$.
hypotheses_covered: a is a member of the list l
p a = false for that element
replaced:
If some element $a$ of a list $l$ satisfies $p(a) = \mathrm{false}$, then $l.\mathrm{all}\,p$
is false.
